title: Which RPG maker do you recommend using?

posts.author: Shironagi
posts.body: I have several RPG Maker engines, like MV and MZ, and although I've learned a few things about these engines, I would like to start creating a game. However, I can't decide which one to choose. I want to see which one offers more benefits so I can start brainstorming ideas for a game, but I'm not sure which one I should pick.

posts.author: Fievol
posts.body: So I'm also new to RPG Maker but I'm really enjoying MZ. I can't speak about too many of the specifics meaningfully, but I've used game engines like Unity, Unreal, and GameMaker. So speaking from that experience I think MZ was the best engine for starting out. It felt very friendly and not too overwhelming. Additionally it has plenty of extra features when you are ready for the more complex stuff. Definitely great for the small RPG I'm making.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
I am personally stuck on MV and even though I own MZ, I am not tempted to switch just yet. This is because I have a large collection of plugins, which are not all compatible with MZ, and buying MZ plugins to replace them, is quite pricey, since, will, I'm talking about 100's of plugins. And money isn't even the worst... But having to relearn all the plugins is just something I don't want to get into right now.
However, if you don't have that problem, and you own both engines, then go with the most recent one, which is MZ.
Edit: You ask which offers more benefits: MZ. Pretty much everything MV does, MZ does as well. But MZ has new features MV doesn't have.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
There are quite a few posts that ask this same question and there are comparison videos as well if you search for them.
All I can say is that I researched this 3 years ago when I was first starting and ultimately I decided on MZ. I haven't regretted that decision.
I haven't really used plugins except what comes with MZ and a few custom plugins that people on this forum helped me with. But I wouldn't give up the TextPicture and ButtonPicture plugins that come with MZ for anything.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Since you own both engines, you can take all the assets from MV and add them to your collection in MZ. Make sure you rename them first. Otherwise they will replace the files with the same filename. I just simply add "_MV" to all the MV filenames and "_MZ" to the MZ filenames.
Not just graphics, btw... Music too. (Also, delete the MP4 files, only copy the OGG files, unless you plan to develop for mobile) Saves up a lot of space, and improved your PC performance when working in those folders. At least on a windows computer.
I know none of this was the question, but I thought I'd mention it anyway. At least now you didn't buy MV for nothing, the assets are absolutely worth it, specially if you are new to RPG maker.
Oh, and keep MV installed. There is something you can still use it for, and that is the character generator, to create more characters for your game. The parts for those characters can not be transferred to MV without problems. But the characters you create with them can!!
both MV and MZ have a generator that allowed you to create a great scala of characters, even more if you add more generator parts (by the community, or bought DLC)
With 2 generators, you are set for the next 203734 characters you need. If you want to use the default graphics style, that is. If not, then both generators are useless.
You say you own more engines, right? You can not simply take graphics from older RPG makers and just add them to MZ with all the other graphics. They are out of scale and they are drawn in a completely different styles. It will not work unless you rescale, and that would be ugly.
Music, however, you can take from the older engines, as long as they are in .ogg format. (or MP4 if you develop for mobile, but I hardly doubt that. In all my years I never ever spoke to someone who actually has a mobile game made with RPG maker.)

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
The tl;dr version is MZ has more editor features, particularly a better map editor and MV is cheaper and has more plugins (also Yanfly vs VisuStella, Yanfly suite is a lot cheaper than VS suite and the code is open so you can edit or get help editing them to your heart's desire).
If you go MV there is an iOS app you can use with your project that has the same map editor features that MZ has, or if you have both you can use MZ as a map editor for an MV project while keeping access to all the MV plugins.

posts.author: Lionbarrel
posts.body:
I second the RMMV  as well, but I have been messing around with the XP as and Have to say if you're willing to read literal mountains to old form post and discussions about RPG Maker of that time. You'll be surprised what you are able to do.  With xp.
It's absolutely ginormous amount of gorgeous assets, music and pretty imagitative ways to use the engine; with plugin and without.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
Seconding XP! I started with it, and never stopped. I adore the mapping system and the default graphics style. But using an old engine does definitely present its own challenges--a lot of the old resources have been lost to time.
Of the newer engines, my vote is MZ. I hated the mapping system from VX through MV--it felt like I had very little control of my maps because I couldn't manually choose which layer I was placing a tile on. MZ's mapping system is much more flexible. You can use it in Auto Layering mode if you liked the VX-MV system, or you can use it in Manual Layering mode if you want to be sure something behaves a certain way. And you can swap freely between them, if overall you prefer Auto but there's something that's just not quite stacking up the way you want.
Also, the price of XP is hard to argue with. When it goes on sale, it's only $2.50 US. As
Avery details here
, it's well worth picking up even if you choose not to make your game in it!

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
If you are new to programming and don't know any coding yet, then (I've been told) JavaScript is the easiest to learn by yourself.
MV and MZ games are made with JavaScript.
If you already know some (or a lot) coding, you should look-up the language per engine. Choose the engine with the language you're most comfortable with. This will give you max freedom to customize your games.
I know VX and VX Ace are written in Ruby. I don't know about the older engines, but should not be hard to find.
